name: head injury overview
title: A head injury is a trauma patient first: the primary survey and the Glasgow Coma Scale grade it; a severe injury is acted on for herniation and sent for a STAT CT, which tells epidural, acute subdural, contusion, intracerebral hemorrhage and diffuse axonal injury or traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage apart, each with its own surgical rule; a concussion is a clinical diagnosis managed by removal, rest and a graded return

root.title: Head injury: a TRAUMA patient first
lines: A airway + C-spine precautions · B breathing · C circulation: large-bore IV, bloods for coagulopathy · D disability: neurological exam + Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) · E expose other injuries
GCS grades it: SEVERE 3-8 · MODERATE 9-12 · MILD 13-14 · MINOR 15

groups.title: SEVERE traumatic brain injury
lines: edema, vasodilation, vascular congestion, hematoma → ↑ intracranial pressure → HERNIATION

pres.title: Herniating? Act, then a STAT CT
lines: • UNCAL: same-side fixed dilated pupil (third nerve) + opposite-side weakness
• TONSILLAR: medulla compressed → Cushing's triad (hypertension, bradycardia, apnea) · fatal
• intubate · head of the bed up · IV mannitol or 3% saline

head: h
Acute subdural hematoma
dura ↔ arachnoid
torn BRIDGING VEINS
clue: • a fall, head strikes a broad surface

head: h
Cerebral contusion
COUP under the impact
CONTRECOUP opposite it
clue: • e.g. confusion, personality change, loss of smell
inv: usually several · repeat CT at 24-48 h: 20% bleed later

head: h
Intracerebral hemorrhage
deceleration or contact
frontal, temporal lobes
clue: A confluent bleed in the brain
• blood dissects the brain around it

head: h
Diffuse axonal injury · traumatic SAH
ACCELERATION injury
often co-exist
clue: LOC at the scene → PERSISTENT coma
• axonal injury is 50% of severe brain injury
inv: grey-white junction, corpus callosum, pons · hard to see

head: h
Concussion
rotational acceleration · NO impact needed
81-92% no LOC · helmets don't prevent it
inv: no CT, MRI, blood test or EEG · SCAT5: 1 of 22 symptoms
tx: 3 · return to PLAY after full-time school + medical clearance
